notes: pitch, h and dk_max have at least three agreeing clusters for every size M4-M24. Width across flats s is split for M10 / M12 / M14: 16 / 18 / 21 mm on fasteners.eu (+itafasteners copy), globalfastener (2014 and 2021 editions) and westfieldfasteners, but 17 / 19 / 22 mm on schrauben-lexikon, boltport and nfgab (and SW 17 / SW 19 on keller-kalmbach article pages for M10 / M12) - three or more clusters on each side, so neither value can be published and the three rows are dropped (catalog keys s and dk_max are both needed by the drawing, so the rows go rather than the column; the alternative rectangle of the same size is 12 sizes x pitch, h, dk_max without s). For M22 the split is 4 to 2 (34 mm: fasteners.eu, globalfastener, westfieldfasteners, boltport; 32 mm: schrauben-lexikon, nfgab) and 34 is kept; note that keller-kalmbach sells M22 both as 'SW 32' (A2 article) and 'SW 34' (A4 article) - these appear in the article titles only, not in a table, and are not counted. globalfastener's DIN 1587-1987 page shows both widths side by side for M10, M12, M14 and M22 (old 17/19/22/32 with dk 16/18/21/31, new 16/18/21/34 with dk 15/17/20/33), which explains the split as old edition versus current edition. dk: fasteners.eu, westfieldfasteners (coarse page), fasten.it, schrauben-lexikon and globalfastener-1987 label it 'max'; globalfastener's 2014 and 2021 pages and westfield's fine-thread page label the same numbers 'min = nominal size' - the numbers agree, the max/min wording does not (kept under the candidate key dk_max because >= 3 clusters say max). keller-kalmbach article pages show the same dk numbers without max/min (not counted for dk_max). Extra columns that also reach 3 clusters (t_min, t_max, e/s/h minimum for product grade A, w_min) are in capnut.evidence.json only; they are not candidates of the current table. | dk column label carries no max/min: four clusters label the same numbers max, the 2014/2021 globalfastener pages and one Westfield page label them min = nominal.

verification.checks_done: Verifier re-fetched every page itself on 2026-11-11 with curl (browser UA, 2.5 s pause per host; HTTP 200 for all; globalfastener detail_400 needed one retry after a 403), wrote its own stdlib HTML table reader (vt.py, gf.py, obs.py) and counting script (count.py) without using the researcher's raw/, extracted tables or scripts. Drawings that define bare symbols (schrauben-lexikon gifs, nfgab pngs) were fetched and viewed. Lead decisions applied: amesweb (calculator) not a source; a rival value printed by 2+ independent lineages removes the row; cells of another standard printed under the target title (verified equal to that standard's table) are neither support nor rival; pages reproducing the standard's text (boltport ISO 4035) excluded. A cluster whose own pages give two different values for a cell is not counted for it. Largest rectangle (cells, then rows) chosen among column subsets that contain the drawing keys. Re-counted 9 x 4 candidate cells; kept 8 x 4; per-cell clusters in capnut.verify.md.
